minor_characters.name: Toots (Judge Miller’s Japanese pug)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly described at Judge Miller’s estate in Ch 001 as one of the pampered house dogs Buck ignores.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He provides local color for Buck’s old life but has no bearing on the plot or Buck’s development.

minor_characters.name: Ysabel (Judge Miller’s Mexican hairless)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly described at Judge Miller’s estate in Ch 001 as another house dog Buck ignores.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Like Toots, she is decorative background that can be cut without affecting story or theme.

minor_characters.name: Mollie and Alice (Judge Miller’s daughters)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named once in Ch 001 as girls Buck escorts on rambles around the estate.
minor_characters.reason_removable: They serve only to illustrate Buck’s former gentility, which the synopsis already establishes.

minor_characters.name: Elmo (Buck’s father)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named in Ch 001 as Judge Miller’s former companion and Buck’s St. Bernard sire.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Buck’s parentage is trivia that does not alter his arc from civilization to primordial mastery.

minor_characters.name: Shep (Buck’s mother)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named in Ch 001 as a Scotch shepherd and Buck’s dam.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Lineage detail is unnecessary to the plot or themes preserved in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Billee
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Introduced in Ch 002 as a good-natured husky; later whimpers in camps and is killed by Hal in Ch 005.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His named presence can be collapsed into unnamed team hardship without changing Buck’s story.

minor_characters.name: Joe
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Introduced in Ch 002 as Billee’s sour brother who resists discipline.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His traits are used to show team dynamics that can be conveyed without a named character.

minor_characters.name: Pike
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Introduced in Ch 002 as a malingering thief whose slyness teaches Buck to steal.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Buck’s learning to steal can be narrated generally without keeping Pike as a distinct character.

minor_characters.name: Dub
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Appears from Ch 002 as a blunderer often punished and later shot under Hal in Ch 005.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is incidental to team wear-and-tear that the synopsis already compresses.

minor_characters.name: Dolly
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A team dog who goes mad and chases Buck in Ch 003 before being killed with an axe.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her episode is an optional shock beat that does not affect the Spitz-Buck showdown or later plot.

minor_characters.name: Teek
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A native husky added at Rink Rapids in Ch 004 and later with Hal’s team in Ch 005.
minor_characters.reason_removable: As an extra team addition, he can be omitted without changing Buck’s arc or the synopsis’ beats.

minor_characters.name: Koona
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Another native husky added with Teek in Ch 004 who later dies under Hal’s mismanagement in Ch 005.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Like Teek, he contributes only surplus detail to the team roster.

minor_characters.name: Jim O’Brien
minor_characters.appearances_summary: In Ch 006, a Mastodon King who lends Thornton money to cover Matthewson’s wager.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The lending detail can be elided while preserving the wager itself, which the synopsis already includes.

minor_characters.name: Skookum Bench King (unnamed onlooker)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: In Ch 006, a wealthy spectator who tries to buy Buck after the sled feat.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His bid is colorful but inconsequential to the outcome or themes.

subplots.name: Starving village huskies raid the Lake Le Barge camp
subplots.reason_removable: This chaotic interlude adds hardship and delays the Spitz fight but is not needed to understand the eventual moonlit rabbit chase and Buck’s victory.

subplots.name: Dolly’s madness and pursuit of Buck
subplots.reason_removable: It is a harrowing standalone incident that neither changes Buck’s arc nor figures in the synopsis’ required beats.

subplots.name: Skaguay ‘bad men’ shootout that diverts public attention
subplots.reason_removable: A town-color anecdote that does not involve Buck’s choices or affect any later event.

subplots.name: Horse‑hide trade at Five Fingers
subplots.reason_removable: The grim detail underscores Hal/Charles/Mercedes’ incompetence, which the synopsis already conveys without this specific episode.

subplots.name: Scrambling the stake for the Eldorado wager (Jim O’Brien’s loan)
subplots.reason_removable: Who fronts the money is logistics that can be skipped while keeping the feat, the wager with Matthewson, and its consequences.

digressions.topic: Extended catalog of Judge Miller’s estate and the house pets (Toots, Ysabel, terriers) and amenities
digressions.reason_removable: It is scene‑setting excess that can be compressed to a line about Buck’s pampered life without loss of plot or theme.

digressions.topic: Nocturnal husky ‘old song’ meditation in Dawson
digressions.reason_removable: A lyrical aside on ancestral sadness that does not alter events or Buck’s decisions already covered in the synopsis.

digressions.topic: Philosophical passage on the ecstasy of the chase before the rabbit run
digressions.reason_removable: The rhapsody is thematic embroidery; the rabbit chase and ensuing fight read clearly without it.

digressions.topic: Lost Cabin asides: ancient blazed path to nowhere and the Hudson’s Bay flintlock anecdote
digressions.reason_removable: Historical-curiosity vignettes that do not affect the partners’ failure to find the cabin or their discovery of the rich valley.
